newsitem.title: UK: BOE's George calls for sustainable UK tax policy.
newsitem.headline: BOE's George calls for sustainable UK tax policy.

text.p: Fiscal policy must be run on a sustainable basis and not place excessive demands on monetary policy, Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Monday.

"A key consideration is that fiscal policy should be sustainable into the medium and longer-term," he said in a speech prepared for delivery to India's central bank, the Reserve Bank of India, in Bombay.
"It is also important that fiscal policy should not place an excessive load on monetary policy to maintain macro-economic stability."
In Britain, Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke will deliver his budget on November 26, the last before elections due by May 1997.
With his ruling Conservative Party lagging in the opinion polls, Clarke will come under intense pressure to cut taxes to woo back disaffected voters.
He will also be keen not to raise interest rates in the run-up to the election. That would push mortgage rates up and about two-thirds of British households own their own properties.
Nonetheless, George has stated his preference for official interest rates to be at 6.00 percent, not 5.75 at the past two monthly monetary meetings with Clarke.
In his speech in Bombay, George said signs of fiscal and monetary slippage were likely to be punished by the financial markets.

"It cannot be assumed that inflation will in future erode the real burden of fiscal imprudence as it has in the past, not least because today's more sophisticated markets are liable to impose interest rate penalties more aggressively if they sense a risk of either monetary or fiscal indiscipline," he said.
